$schema_note: Diacritic + context disambiguation rules for high-frequency Arabic function-word homographs that norm() collapses. Each rule keys on the harakah of the CONTENT letter (read AFTER any و/ف proclitic), never the first letter. Consume with tools.normalize_ar: haraka_on(tok, letter), shadda_on(tok, letter), is_man_who(tok). FATHA=064E, KASRA=0650, DAMMA=064F, SHADDA=0651. A rule emits decision_if_A / decision_if_B; if the diacritic is absent (undiacritized input) emit the pending fallback. PENDING beats a wrong gloss.

distinguish_by.also: shadda_on(tok, 'ن') guards the verb مَنَّ 'to bestow'

decision_if_A.when: no kasra on mīm (fatḥa or bare) AND no shadda on nūn
decision_if_A.reason: fatḥa (or bare) on the mīm content letter → pronoun, not the preposition مِنْ

decision_if_B.when: kasra on mīm (incl. وَمِنَ where the و proclitic shifts the harakah right)
decision_if_B.reason: kasra on the mīm content letter → preposition; the leading و/ف does not move the decision letter

pending_fallback.note: undiacritized input: مَن/مِن indistinguishable without the content-letter harakah

rules.guard: وَمِنَ is NOT وَمَن; وَمَنَّ (shadda on nūn) is the verb 'to bestow', neither pronoun nor preposition

distinguish_by.also: sukūn on mīm marks لَمْ; fatḥa on mīm marks لِمَ

decision_if_A.when: fatḥa on lām (and the following verb is jussive)
decision_if_A.reason: negation of the past via jussive; e.g. لَمْ يَلِدْ

pending_fallback.note: without the lām harakah, لَمْ 'did not' and لِمَ 'why' are not separable

decision_if_A.reason: fatḥa-seat hamza → أَنْ/أَنَّ; light أَنْ takes subjunctive, أَنَّ (shadda) takes a noun-clause

decision_if_B.reason: kasra-seat hamza → إِنَّ/إِنْ; shadda marks the emphatic, light إِنْ is conditional or negating

pending_fallback.note: if norm() dropped the hamza seat, re-read with norm_strict before deciding أَنْ vs إِنَّ

distinguish_by.signal: kasra cluster on nūn → أَنِّي; fatḥa on nūn → أَنَّى
distinguish_by.also: final yāʾ ـِي (1sg pronoun) vs final alif-maqṣūra ـَى

decision_if_A.reason: kasra cluster on the nūn; e.g. أَنِّي أَنَا الْغَفُورُ

decision_if_B.reason: fatḥa on nūn → adverbial أَنَّى, not the pronoun-bearing أَنِّي

decision_if_B.gloss: nay / by no means / not so

distinguish_by.signal: occurrence-specific CONTEXTUAL FRAME, not a diacritic — مَا carries no content-letter mark that separates relative from negation, so the DISCRIMINATORS haraka registry does not apply to this rule

rules.axis_note: This rule discriminates ONLY relative-vs-negation — the two-way axis its own frame_table can actually examine. It is a faithful restatement of the fixture's 2-way rule (tools/skill_fixtures/skill_rules.py:_ma_neg_rel_corrected), never a complete مَا function classifier. A frame this table selects a candidate FOR settles nothing about the five OTHER attested مَا functions below; they are never rejected merely because this axis picked an in-axis winner — they stay unresolved, out of this axis's examination scope entirely (`not_examined_by_this_axis`), exactly like an absent observation.

مَا is the mafʿūl of a preceding transitive verb and the clause continues with a noun

مَا is not the object of a preceding transitive verb, but the clause it heads continues with a noun

rules.$surface_note: 'فَ' below is a documentary EXAMPLE surface for this rule's prose, not a matching key — exactly like maa_relative_vs_negation above, no code path looks up a surface string here; the frame_table governs by OCCURRENCE-SPECIFIC contextual frame, never by surface identity. فاء carries no content-letter diacritic distinction of its own (always fatḥa), so this rule's signal is structural, not haraka.

distinguish_by.signal: occurrence-specific CONTEXTUAL FRAME: the mood marking of the following/linked verb, and what element (if any) actually licenses that mood — never fa's bare presence
distinguish_by.also: a frame this table does not bind to EXACTLY one function is never guessed at; both/all rivals stay pending, exactly like an absent observation. fa's own function is ALWAYS decided separately from any following particle's function (e.g. a following مَا) — this table never reports a blended label.

rules.axis_note: This rule discriminates fa's own function among three members: istiʾnāfiyya (resumptive, opens a new clause with no mood claim), sababiyya (fā' al-sababiyya, the causative/result clause whose following imperfect is licensed into the subjunctive by an implied أَنْ — fa itself is the licensing CONTEXT, never the stated governor), and rābiṭa (a bare linking fa before an apodosis/next clause whose own mood, if any, is governed by something else entirely, e.g. lām al-amr — fa is explicitly NOT the mood governor in this member). ʿāṭifa (plain listing coordination) is an attested fa function this table does not discriminate; it stays out-of-axis. Two frames (narrative_perfect_no_mood_question, linked_to_separate_particle_component) are marked unique_within_axis:false precisely because their own observable is equally compatible with the out-of-axis ʿāṭifa reading — they cannot honestly exclude it, so they stay pending rather than silently selecting an in-axis winner; only result_after_prohibition_or_negation_with_visible_subjunctive and linked_to_lam_al_amr_jussive_apodosis carry a structural signal (the licensed subjunctive; the lām al-amr apodosis) that a plain listing ʿāṭifa could not itself produce, so those two stay genuinely discriminating.

Candidate-only, fixture-producer posture — see the bank file's own header note.

frame_table.reason: fa links to a perfect-tense narrative verb with no mood to license, e.g. فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ; this observable is equally consistent with fa being a plain listing ʿāṭifa (out-of-axis, functions_not_discriminated) coordinating the clause, so istinafiyya is never selected from this frame alone — the axis stays pending with every in-axis rival preserved until a discriminator that actually excludes ʿāṭifa is supplied

fa follows a prohibition/negation/request and the next imperfect verb carries a visible subjunctive (fatḥa) ending; fā' al-sababiyya is the causative/result frame, but the subjunctive is licensed by an implied أَنْ, not by fa directly, e.g. فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا
fa merely links to an apodosis/command clause opened by lām al-amr + jussive verb; the jussive is governed by the lām, never by fa, e.g. فَلْيُؤَدِّ

fa links/resumes and is immediately followed by a DISTINCT particle (e.g. مَا) that carries its own separate function, decided independently by that particle's own rule (never fused into one 'fa_plus_x' label), e.g. فَمَا كَانَ لَكُم; this observable does not itself exclude fa being a plain listing ʿāṭifa (out-of-axis) before that particle, so rabita is never selected from this frame alone — the axis stays pending with every in-axis rival preserved
frame_table.component_boundary: this frame never asserts or requires the linked particle's own function; that is a separate decision

frame_table.reason: the observed frame does not establish whether fa opens a genuinely new resumptive clause or merely links to what follows; both readings stay open rather than defaulting to either

recognized_unmapped_frames.reason: the source mechanism can report fa joining two like items in a simple list (ʿāṭifa) — a real, closed-vocabulary frame an observer may legitimately report, but this table's axis does not discriminate ʿāṭifa from its sisters, so it is recognized but deliberately left UNMAPPED rather than folded into istinafiyya or rabita. A recognized-but-unmapped frame stays pending with pending_reason=frame_row_missing — distinct from an off-vocabulary caller error — and never defaults to a function.

pending_fallback.note: no frame observation, or a frame value outside this table AND outside recognized_unmapped_frames, stays pending; a frame is never inferred from the caller's own conclusion label, and fa's bare surface presence is never treated as evidence of any one function
